title: Power Rankings: Cleveland climbs back to the top
heading: 2008-09 Power Rankings: Week 22
author: Marc Stein

rankings.summaryHtml: Something else to boost Cleveland's case/title chances: Only four teams can stop the Cavs from winning a championship and three of them (thanks to Bynum, Garnett and Duncan/Ginobili) still face major injury uncertainty.
rankings.summaryText: Something else to boost Cleveland's case/title chances: Only four teams can stop the Cavs from winning a championship and three of them (thanks to Bynum, Garnett and Duncan/Ginobili) still face major injury uncertainty.

rankings.summaryHtml: You'd typically pardon an L in Atlanta knowing what the Hawks are like at home. In this case, though, L.A. has to take a hit, failing to get to 80 points right after the Hawks fell to the Timmy-less Spurs and KG-less Celts.

rankings.summaryHtml: You probably know what we're going to say, but the safety-first committee (of one) can't help it. We urge Doc to shelve KG until the playoffs, banking on the idea he can use the first round to get his sharpness back.

rankings.summaryHtml: A deserved return to Denver's old No. 6 perch. Opposition injuries have certainly helped in a few cases, but the Nuggets have now racked up road W's in Boston, San Antonio, Orlando, New Orleans and Dallas twice.

rankings.summaryHtml: Maybe it's contradictory to say this team has been stabilized by T-Mac's exit but that we also remain skeptical of the Rockets as a playoff entity. You tell us, though. How do they win over skeptics before winning a round?

rankings.summaryHtml: We thought Dallas had an opening to get out of the dreaded No. 8 spot with two cracks at the Hornets and Chandler (and possibly Peja) expected to miss both. Then N.O. beat the Spurs without those two and Posey.

rankings.summaryHtml: Home dates with the Jazz, Lakers and Nuggets. Five more road games to go with those three toughies at home. But you know what? Utah's closing schedule is still worse, so maybe Portland can hang on to the No. 5 seed.

rankings.summaryHtml: Does a win over the Lakers after their aforementioned stumbles against Duncan-less San Antonio and Garnett-less Boston restore the Hawks' home-court fear factor? Another question only the playoffs will answer.

rankings.summaryHtml: The Jazz are 1-14 on the road against teams with a winning record ... and that one was way back on Nov. 11 at Philly. Which is a stat you can't blow off when all six of their remaining roadies are against winning teams.

rankings.summaryHtml: The good news: No. 8 Dallas has been presented with three very winnable games this week before the teetering No. 9 Suns arrive for Sunday's showdown. The bad news: Read the comment next to the Hornets' logo.

rankings.summaryHtml: This is starting to feel like 2005-06, when Chicago closed with a 12-2 rush to go 41-41 before pushing the eventual champs from Miami to six games in Round 1. At least that's what longtime Bulls observer Sam Smith says.

rankings.summaryHtml: We said it a bunch: No way AI goes into free agency, in this economy, with the world thinking he tanked the last 25 games to avoid sixth-man duty. But we also have to admit we didn't expect AI to sit out as long as he did.

rankings.summaryHtml: Sometimes nostalgia is good, like playing at the Spectrum one last time. And sometimes nostalgia ruins your weekend, like Larry Brown's Bobs winning Friday in Philly, followed by Philly's loss in Detroit in AI's return.

rankings.summaryHtml: The last time Shaq missed the playoffs -- with Orlando at 41-41 in his rookie season -- his team won the lottery as a consolation prize. Knowing how lucky the Suns are, though, do you think that's even an option?

rankings.summaryHtml: The Bobcats have never played a game in April that mattered. That will finally change this week in spite of a loss at Washington that realistically dooms Larry's Bobs now that the Pistons have finally awakened.

rankings.summaryHtml: The umpteenth Pacers paradox of the season: Our man Troy Murphy strains his knee on the final play of the morning shootaround ... and then Indy goes out and beats Miami anyway without Murphy or Dunleavy.

rankings.summaryHtml: It says a lot about what piques national interest in 2009 when Charlie Villanueva's Twitter account generates reams more coverage than all the injuries and everything else that's happened in Milwaukee this season.

rankings.summaryHtml: Everyone knows Brook Lopez was an absolute steal at No. 10. His rookie prowess is a heartening counter to the massive Yi Jianlian disappointment. Doesn't mean he's worthy of passing Rose on our ROY ballot, though.

rankings.summaryHtml: Par for the season, eh? Not until our Raps fall 20 games under .500 -- and not until some of the locals start openly souring on Bosh -- do they string four wins together for the first time since (yikes) December of last season.

rankings.summaryHtml: The ballyhooed Summer of 2010 can't get here fast enough, huh? The Knicks' depressing March swoon out of the playoff race has clinched their eighth straight losing season. One more and they set a franchise record.

rankings.summaryHtml: Can't let it go. Can't stop wondering, even if Chandler is injured, why the Thunder didn't just go through with the trade, sit him for the rest of the season and try to get him right for the final two seasons on his contract.
